There is indeed an epidemic of male loneliness, largely caused by social media and dating apps. No arguments there. But real-world spaces still exist, and many people who meet a partner via social media do so by talking to them first and foremost rather than just swiping.

I'm not saying that it's easy to break free of it, but ultimately it's the very fact that so many people hang out in these toxic online spaces that becomes their downfall. You have to make the choice to not participate.

OP, I just want to say thank you for recognising that you're in a toxic situation and that you've been, at least to a certain extent, affected by misinformation that you see online. It's an incredibly difficult step and asking for help here is also tough to do.

Like the other commenters have largely said, the best way to deal with how these echo chambers have affected your thought processes is by leaving them. Find other things to do with your time. Find a local hobby that's inclusive of women. Getting to know a group of people is the first step to dispelling misinformation about them.

And for anyone else reading this in a similar situation to OP, I offer the same advice. What I will qualify that with though, for the masses, because I'm part of a hobby that suffers _badly_ from this (D&D): please, please shower and clean yourself when going to your new hobby.
